output.brief: The rise is not mainly a handler problem. On 1 September Harlow Bay also switched bag-tag stock to Fennick Labels. Tags printed on it fail automatic reading about 12% of the time, against 1.5% on the old Brackwater stock. Corvane's transfer tags and Pelion's tags, read by the same equipment and worked by the same Tessaly crews, stayed near 1.4%. Pelion's mishandling rate did not rise. On 14–16 October, counter tags printed on Brackwater stock from stores failed at only 1.6%. Kiosk tags printed on Fennick the same days failed at 12.1%. The extra unread bags go to the manual encode desk. Their wait there rose from about 7 to 33 minutes, and 91% of the bags that missed their flight reached the lateral after it had closed. Do not send the breach notice or withhold the fee, because the evidence points away from Tessaly as the main cause. Switch counters and kiosks back to the Brackwater stock now. About five weeks of it is in stores and the contract runs to 31 December. Then see whether the fault is the stock itself or the printer heat setting. The Teyra bulletin and the kiosk service reports would help. Hold off on a defect claim against Fennick until then. Asking HBAA for an extra encode workstation in the evening is a reasonable stopgap. Tessaly's crew experience may still matter somewhat, but it is not shown to drive the rise. I'm fairly confident in the tag-stock finding and less sure whether the stock or the printer setting is at fault.
